podcast.body: On December 17, 1977, during a last-minute appearance on Saturday Night Live, Elvis Costello was explicitly instructed by the show's producers not to perform "Radio Radio" due to its critical stance on radio broadcasting and NBC's ownership of radio stations. Despite initially agreeing to play "Less Than Zero," he famously stopped that song midway through and launched into the forbidden "Radio Radio," defying the network's censorship. "I'm sorry, ladies and gentlemen, there's no reason to do this song here. Radio radio."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
